entry_point.discipline_context: Use potential energy, equilibrium, and numerical relaxation to motivate a design or simulation objective over configuration variables.
entry_point.rationale: Mechanical engineering students can connect a downhill energy picture with a gradient step before formalising the same idea for a general objective.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The analogy is framing only: an arbitrary objective need not be physical potential energy, and optimisation iterates are not necessarily time evolution or a physically stable trajectory.

chapter_sequence.title: From equilibrium to an optimisation problem
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce objective functions, unconstrained minimisation, stationarity, and second-order optimality checks through a carefully bounded energy analogy.

chapter_sequence.title: Geometry: smoothness, convexity, and conditioning
chapter_sequence.purpose: Define the global inequalities and Hessian interpretations that control local geometry and convergence reasoning.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and choosing a step
chapter_sequence.purpose: State the canonical update, constant choices, exact line search, and Armijo backtracking, then connect the descent lemma to implementation.

chapter_sequence.title: What convergence guarantees actually say
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present the convex sublinear and strongly convex contraction results with their separate step sizes and assumptions.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum and acceleration
chapter_sequence.purpose: Compare Heavy Ball and the approved NAG recurrence, including the exact scope of their convergence statements.

chapter_sequence.title: Stochastic and adaptive gradient methods
chapter_sequence.purpose: Model empirical objectives and gradient noise, explain SGD step schedules and error floors, and introduce AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam semantics.

chapter_sequence.title: Second-order optimisation: Newton's method
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce the second-order Taylor model, Newton linear solve, and local quadratic convergence without overstating global behaviour.

chapter_sequence.title: BFGS and an engineering workflow
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain the BFGS secant condition and inverse-Hessian update, then consolidate method selection and checks in executable Python.

implementation_strategy: Use short NumPy-free Python examples with lists and scalar/quadratic objectives so the code runs in a minimal interpreter; connect each operation to the displayed update and report objective values, not unsupported claims about physical time.
assessment_strategy: Ask learners to identify assumptions behind a claimed rate, derive one update from a gradient, compare a noisy trajectory with a deterministic one, and explain why Newton or BFGS may need a line search or a good initial point.
